dedupe_keys.name: cyder cyber physical co simulation platform for distributed energy resources

description: CyDER is a co-simulation platform for studying how distributed energy resources such as rooftop solar affect distribution and transmission grids together. It was developed at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory by Thierry Nouidui, Jonathan Coignard, Christoph Gehbauer, Michael Wetter, Jhi-Young Joo and Evangelos Vrettos, and described in a 2018 paper, because growing distributed resources cause reverse power flows and stability issues that single-domain tools and distribution operators cannot see as a whole. CyDER couples domain-specific simulation tools through the Functional Mock-up Interface standard, and its README names three pillars: quasi-static time series co-simulation and optimisation, real-time data acquisition, and hardware-in-the-loop use, with the aim of working alongside utility interconnection planning tools. Coverage is not tied to a place; it is a general framework. The source code is accessible on GitHub and the paper supplement is on figshare under CC BY 4.0, at no cost. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0. Simulation uses are co-simulating transmission, distribution and distributed resources for planning and operation studies. Related records: platform-helics is a more actively maintained co-simulation framework.
